selected.lesson_subject: FGCP HA checksum mismatch caused by per-member dynamic WWAN IPv6 addresses
selected.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FGCP configuration checksum comparison incorrectly treats modem-learned, per-member WWAN IPv6 addresses as static synchronized configuration; the distinct dynamic address is not a data-plane HA failure.
selected.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Each LTE modem independently learns a provider IPv6 address; HA checksum engine includes the dynamic address in its configuration comparison; member checksums diverge and GUI/CLI reports out-of-sync although heartbeat and policy sync remain operational.
selected.failure_class: False-positive HA configuration drift caused by dynamic cellular IPv6 state being included in checksum eligibility.
selected.evidence_pattern: get system ha status shows Configuration Status out-of-sync and different checksum dumps; HBDEV/MONDEV statistics remain healthy; member WWAN IPv6 addresses differ; traffic and new configuration synchronization continue.
selected.remediation_path: Do not run diagnose ha checksum recalculate on affected devices because it can temporarily overwrite the peer WWAN IPv6 address. Verify firmware parity, heartbeat counters, traffic and ordinary config propagation; treat the mismatch as the documented exception and upgrade when the vendor fix is available (Community article says FortiOS 8.0.3+; schedule may change).
selected.question_fingerprint: Distinguish a dynamic WWAN IPv6 checksum exception from a real HA sync failure and select the safe non-destructive response.
selected.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Two FGCP peers each with a separate LTE modem and unique dynamic IPv6 address; shared heartbeat link; checksum comparison path highlighted as false mismatch while forwarding paths remain healthy.
selected.semantic_uniqueness_review: No prior FortiGate record teaches dynamic WWAN IPv6 in HA checksums. Nearest prior IPv6 lessons concern ND proxy/SLAAC; they are different packet/neighbor mechanisms. No prior record covers per-member modem-learned IPv6 state in FGCP checksum eligibility.

selected.lesson_subject: SQLite WAL corruption in ADOM databases after 7.6.7 upgrade: integrity diagnostics and recovery boundaries
selected.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: SQLite write-ahead-log corruption physically malforms per-ADOM databases; integrity checks distinguish corruption from policy-package inconsistency; full system backup and database restoration are separate from ADOM revision rollback.
selected.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: FortiManager 7.6.7 upgrade introduces SQLite 3.50.4 WAL bug; ADOM integrity_check reports missing index rows or malformed database; Policy & Objects load and policy pushes fail; recovery requires a known-good pre-upgrade backup/clean upgrade or the Community-reported 7.6.10 recovery command, followed by repeat integrity checks.
selected.failure_class: Persistent ADOM SQLite database corruption after firmware upgrade, causing UI load failures, index errors and policy deployment failures.
selected.evidence_pattern: diagnose pm2 check-integrity all reports pragma integrity_check failures such as database disk image is malformed or row missing from index; diagnose cdb check adom-integrity reports sqlite3_backup_step rc=11; Policy & Objects returns Response with errors.
selected.remediation_path: Before any repair, export and verify a system backup; ensure only one administrator is logged in, no objects are locked and all ADOMs are unlocked in workspace mode. Use official integrity checks to localize failure. The Community article reports diagnose cdb upgrade check recover-corrupted-adomdb in 7.6.10, but the exact recovery command/version was not independently found in the official CLI reference during this run; verify with the installed build and Fortinet Support before use. The official documented diagnose pm2 db-recover global applies to the global database only and requires offline mode/reboot.
selected.question_fingerprint: Identify physical SQLite/WAL corruption from exact integrity output and avoid misusing global-database recovery against an ADOM database.
selected.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Upgrade pipeline feeding SQLite WAL and ADOM database; integrity-check branch; backup verification gate; separate restore/ADOM recovery path; post-recovery recheck.
selected.semantic_uniqueness_review: Prior records cover ADOM revisions, policy package diffs, workspace mode and revision restore. They do not cover SQLite WAL corruption, pragma integrity_check, row/index corruption or physical ADOM database recovery. This is a different failure class and transaction.

selected.lesson_subject: FortiMQ connector: ADOM-scoped blocked-indicator delivery to FortiGate Cloud Fabric Feeds
selected.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiAnalyzer 8.0 FortiMQ connector publishes IP, URL, domain and MAC block indicators to a cloud broker; FortiGate retrieves the feed and policy/profile enforcement remains a separate FortiGate configuration step.
selected.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: An analyst blocks an indicator in an ADOM; block_indicator playbook sends it through the enabled FortiMQ connector; FortiGate on the same FortiCare account consumes Cloud-based Fabric Feed synchronization; the indicator appears in external feeds and a referencing policy/profile denies matching traffic.
selected.failure_class: Indicator marked blocked in analytics but not enforced at the firewall due connector, FortiCare account, ADOM scope, cloud feed synchronization or policy-reference mismatch.
selected.evidence_pattern: FortiMQ connector is enabled and healthy; Block action tooltip names FortiMQ; indicator status and block_indicator playbook execution are visible; FortiGate external feed contains the indicator; a matching test session is denied only when a policy/profile references the feed.
selected.remediation_path: Enable FortiMQ in the target Fabric/FortiGate ADOM; confirm FortiAnalyzer and FortiGate share the same FortiCare account; enable Cloud-based Fabric Feed synchronization on FortiGate; verify correct ADOM membership and feed references in policy/profile. Remember FortiMQ is ADOM-specific and takes priority over FortiManager connector when both are active. The Node2Shell community event handler raises alerts/reports; it does not itself block indicators.
selected.question_fingerprint: Trace the indicator from ADOM to FortiMQ to FortiGate feed and distinguish detection/alerting from actual enforcement.
selected.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Event/log source to FortiAnalyzer ADOM indicator store; block_indicator playbook to FortiMQ cloud; FortiGate feed consumer; separate policy enforcement node; alternate FortiManager connector path shown as fallback.
selected.semantic_uniqueness_review: Prior FortiAnalyzer lessons cover log fetch, event handlers, automation playbooks and report generation. They do not cover FortiMQ's cloud indicator transaction, ADOM-specific scoping, same-FortiCare requirement or FortiGate Fabric Feed consumption.

selected.lesson_subject: FortiSwitchOS 8.0 DNS over TLS with optional CA validation and cache-memory semantics
selected.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiSwitchOS 8.0.0 changes the switch's own system DNS client from cleartext UDP/TCP 53 to DNS over TLS on TCP 853; an optional configured server CA enables certificate-chain validation before the TLS session is established.
selected.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: The switch selects primary/secondary DNS server and protocol dot; TCP/853 TLS handshake validates the DNS server certificate only when server-ca-cert is configured; DNS query/response travels inside TLS; local switch functions such as email alerts and URL blocking consume the resolved answer.
selected.failure_class: Encrypted DNS connection failure or false sense of server authentication because DoT is enabled without supported upstream service or without a trusted CA certificate.
selected.evidence_pattern: config system dns shows protocol dot, primary/secondary servers and server-ca-cert; packet capture shows TCP/853 rather than UDP/TCP 53; certificate validation behavior differs when server-ca-cert is absent; dns-cache-limit is measured in KB (default 512) rather than entries.
selected.remediation_path: Confirm the upstream resolver supports DoT on TCP/853; import the correct issuing CA and set server-ca-cert; test DNS resolution and certificate trust separately; verify source-ip and route to resolver; monitor cache size and TTL. Do not assume encryption alone authenticates the resolver when no CA certificate is configured.
selected.question_fingerprint: Distinguish encrypted transport from authenticated resolver identity and interpret the 8.0.0 dns-cache-limit unit change.
selected.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: FortiSwitch management/system DNS client to TCP/853 TLS channel, optional CA trust validation gate, upstream resolver, returned answer to local switch services; cleartext 53 shown as alternate.
selected.semantic_uniqueness_review: No prior FortiSwitch lesson covers system DNS transport or CA validation. The rejected FortiGate DoT inspection candidate is not selected in this report, so this remains the only DoT lesson and does not duplicate a FortiGate transit-inspection topic.

selected.lesson_subject: Wi-Fi 7 Multi-Link Operation on FortiAP K-series: VAP security, radio mapping and standalone behavior
selected.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: 802.11be Multi-Link Operation creates one multi-link device relationship across supported 2.4/5/6 GHz radios and channels; one VAP/SSID and its security profile are applied to selected radios, with model-specific radio limitations.
selected.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Configure a VAP with WPA3-SAE, WPA3 Enterprise Only or OWE and enable mlo; map that VAP to the desired radios in a WTP profile; an MLO-capable client associates with multiple link IDs; in standalone mode, bridge traffic and local authentication allow the AP to continue without the controller.
selected.failure_class: MLO option absent or client falls back to a single link because of unsupported AP/radio/firmware, incompatible security settings, incorrect WTP radio mapping or client capability.
selected.evidence_pattern: diagnose wpa wpad mld reports num_links and link_id values; FortiAP vcfg shows mlo=enabled; sta output shows the client on multiple radio interfaces; a single link does not prove MLO association.
selected.remediation_path: Verify K-series model and radio support, FAP 7.6.3+ and FortiOS 7.6.5 CLI or 8.0.0 GUI support; use supported WPA3/OWE security and SAE H2E-only; apply VAP to intended WTP radios; confirm client MLO capability; for standalone mode enable bridge, local-standalone and local-authentication.
selected.question_fingerprint: Diagnose why a K-series SSID advertises but does not establish multiple links and interpret num_links correctly.
selected.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: One MLD client linked concurrently to three AP radio nodes (2.4/5/6 GHz), all sharing a VAP/security profile; optional FortiGate controller and standalone local-auth path.
selected.semantic_uniqueness_review: Prior wireless records cover SAE_EXT AKM24, MPSK, roaming, airtime fairness, CAPWAP and RF behavior. MLO is the 802.11be multi-link association mechanism, not an AKM/security-suite or roaming feature.

selected.lesson_subject: Local RADIUS PEAP-MSCHAPv2 failures after Windows KB5127648 changes cached NTLMv1 SSO behavior
selected.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiNAC local RADIUS terminates the PEAP outer TLS tunnel and uses MSCHAPv2/Winbind for AD user authentication; the October 2026 Windows update changes cached NTLMv1 SSO credential behavior without changing FortiNAC RADIUS server operation.
selected.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Windows supplicant sends 802.1X EAP through switch/AP NAS to FortiNAC RADIUS; PEAP establishes outer TLS; inner MSCHAPv2 uses cached Windows logon credentials through Winbind/AD; KB5127648 changes BlockNtlmv1SSO default behavior and cached SSO fails while manually entered credentials still work.
selected.failure_class: Endpoint-side cached credential/NTLMv1 SSO policy regression, not a FortiNAC RADIUS protocol or switch authorization failure.
selected.evidence_pattern: Windows OneX Event ID 12014 reports Held State Timeout; failures occur only with Automatically use my Windows logon name and password; manual credentials succeed; EAP-TLS clients are unaffected.
selected.remediation_path: Verify KB5127648 and BlockNtlmv1SSO at HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa\MSV1_0. Community article documents Audit mode DWORD value 0 as a temporary compatibility workaround and uninstall as a confirmed rollback; centrally manage with GPO. Prefer migration to EAP-TLS rather than permanently weakening NTLMv1 SSO protections.
selected.question_fingerprint: Separate PEAP outer TLS, inner MSCHAPv2, Winbind/AD and Windows cached SSO policy to locate the actual failure boundary.
selected.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Windows supplicant to wired/wireless NAS to FortiNAC local RADIUS; PEAP outer TLS wraps inner MSCHAPv2/Winbind-to-AD; Windows cached credential policy highlighted as failing endpoint boundary.
selected.semantic_uniqueness_review: Prior FortiNAC records cover EAP session correlation and local-vs-external RADIUS; a prior FortiNAC-F record covers Winbind domain join. This lesson focuses on Windows endpoint cached NTLMv1 SSO behavior after KB5127648, not RADIUS session correlation or FortiNAC domain join.

selected.lesson_subject: Microsoft Intune NAC-API on-demand registration: MAC-to-DeviceID lookup and Vendor OUI validation
selected.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiNAC-F's Microsoft NAC-API integration replaces full Intune asset-list retrieval with per-host lookup; MAC address resolves an Intune Device ID, then Graph/MDM data is retrieved; valid-MAC/OUI registration is a separate host-admission gate.
selected.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Host discovery creates a pending/rogue record; MDM poll calls Microsoft NAC-API for a single MAC/DeviceID; application permissions allow daemon/background access; returned compliance and host metadata are applied only after MAC passes the Vendor OUI validity check.
selected.failure_class: Intune device is found by the poller but not registered because the endpoint MAC is rejected as invalid by a stale Vendor OUI database; delegated permissions can also force inefficient full-list polling and prevent on-demand lookup.
selected.evidence_pattern: MSInTuneServer debug log shows device discovered but absent from Host View; validmac -mac <MAC_ADDRESS> returns Invalid; after Auto Definition Sync, validmac returns Vendor OUI and manufacturer; new MDM poll registers the host.
selected.remediation_path: Use Microsoft NAC-API with Application Permissions rather than delegated permissions; configure API secret or certificate authentication and required Graph/NAC-API permissions; update Vendor OUI through Agent Update Settings and Auto Definition Sync; rerun validmac and Intune poll. Community article scope labels the shared workflow FortiNAC, while the primary feature guide is FortiNAC-F 7.6.0; the scope mismatch is disclosed.
selected.question_fingerprint: Trace a device discovered by Intune but missing from Host View through NAC-API lookup and the independent MAC/OUI registration gate.
selected.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Endpoint MAC to FortiNAC-F poller; NAC-API single-host DeviceID lookup; Microsoft Graph Intune data response; parallel Vendor OUI validity gate; registered host record only after both branches pass.
selected.semantic_uniqueness_review: Prior FortiNAC-F records cover LDAP host association, directory synchronization, NetFlow, SAML and HA. None covers Microsoft Intune NAC-API per-host retrieval or the Vendor OUI validity gate.

selected.lesson_subject: FortiAuthenticator 8.0.2 HA control-plane separation with dedicated management and heartbeat interfaces
selected.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiAuthenticator 8.0.2 adds a dedicated Heartbeat Interface separate from the renamed Management interface/Management IP; the management plane handles administrator reachability while heartbeat carries HA synchronization and health monitoring.
selected.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Configure cluster management IP and management access on the management interface; select a separate heartbeat interface on each node; peers exchange heartbeat/sync messages over the dedicated network; standby declares peer out-of-service after configured missed-heartbeat threshold and takes over in active-passive cluster mode.
selected.failure_class: HA control-plane coupling or false failover caused by management-network reachability being conflated with heartbeat health, or heartbeat path/threshold misconfiguration.
selected.evidence_pattern: System > Administration > High Availability shows Management interface/IP and Heartbeat Interface; heartbeat interval default 1000 ms and lost threshold default 6000 ms; verify each network independently and observe member role/failover state.
selected.remediation_path: Use separate reachable management and heartbeat networks; ensure heartbeat L2/L3 requirements and firewall rules are met; set interval/threshold deliberately; verify node-specific management default gateway where needed; test failover under controlled conditions and confirm management remains reachable independently.
selected.question_fingerprint: Distinguish administrator access loss from heartbeat loss after management and heartbeat interfaces are decoupled.
selected.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Two FortiAuthenticator nodes with separate management subnet and heartbeat/sync subnet; admin workstation reaches management IPs while peer heartbeat arrows cross isolated heartbeat network; active/standby role transition.
selected.semantic_uniqueness_review: Prior FortiAuthenticator records cover FIDO2, OAuth, SAML certificate rotation, RADIUS/TACACS policy, LDAP and EAP. No prior record covers HA management/heartbeat interface separation. Other products' HA lessons concern different components and failure planes.

selected.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiPAM 1.9.0 adds RADIUS Message-Authenticator attribute generation and response validation; require-message-authenticator defaults enabled and makes the response attribute mandatory.
selected.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: FortiPAM builds a RADIUS authentication request including Message-Authenticator; remote RADIUS server validates the shared-secret-based integrity value and returns a response; FortiPAM validates response Message-Authenticator before accepting remote authentication.
selected.failure_class: RADIUS authentication rejection when the remote server omits or incorrectly calculates Message-Authenticator, or when shared secrets/packet attributes do not match.
selected.evidence_pattern: FortiPAM RADIUS server configuration shows require-message-authenticator enabled; packet capture shows attribute 80 in request/response; authentication succeeds with compliant server and fails when response attribute is absent or invalid.
selected.remediation_path: Keep require-message-authenticator enabled with a RADIUS server that supports the attribute; verify shared secret and packet construction on both sides; use set require-message-authenticator disable only as a temporary interoperability workaround when the server cannot provide the attribute, documenting the integrity reduction and restoring enforcement after server remediation.
selected.question_fingerprint: Explain why Message-Authenticator is an integrity/authenticity check rather than encryption and choose the safe response to a server that omits attribute 80.
selected.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: FortiPAM remote-auth client sends RADIUS request with attribute 80 to RADIUS server; response returns attribute 80; FortiPAM validation gate either accepts or rejects before admin login.
selected.semantic_uniqueness_review: Prior FortiPAM records cover secret creation, checkout locks, TOTP, session recording, gateway chaining, SSH certificate authentication and scheduled jobs. None covers RADIUS attribute 80 generation or response integrity enforcement.

selected.lesson_subject: FortiSIEM Collector High Availability: VRRP leader/follower failover and Supervisor job redistribution
selected.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: Collector HA is a data-collection tier feature separate from Supervisor active-passive HA; a Leader owns a virtual IP via VRRP (on-prem/AWS) or a cloud load balancer fronts Collectors (Azure/GCP), while Supervisor/App Server redistributes event-pull and performance-monitoring jobs.
selected.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Log sources send to a stable VIP; Leader Collector receives logs; Supervisor distributes polling/monitoring jobs among members; on Leader failure the highest-priority Follower takes VIP and jobs are redistributed; on Follower failure App Server moves its jobs to other members.
selected.failure_class: Collector host or process failure causes log loss or polling-job interruption; VRRP or load-balancer health checks may not detect an application process failure when the OS remains reachable.
selected.evidence_pattern: Cluster Config shows HA group, Leader/Follower, VRRP or load balancer and VIP; logs continue to arrive at new Leader; job redistribution occurs when App Server misses task request for 10 minutes; process-down may not trigger VRRP failover.
selected.remediation_path: Keep VIP and Collectors on the same network for VRRP; set priorities and verify failover; use application-aware load-balancer health checks where supported; monitor Collector processes and App Server job queues; account for the documented 10-minute redistribution window and test leader and follower failures separately.
selected.question_fingerprint: Distinguish Collector-tier VRRP failover from Supervisor HA and identify why a process failure may not trigger a VIP move.
selected.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Multiple log sources target a VIP; Leader/Follower Collectors share VRRP or load-balancer front end; Supervisor/App Server distributes pull/monitor jobs; failure arrow moves VIP and jobs to healthy peers.
selected.semantic_uniqueness_review: The prior 2026-11-02 FortiSIEM lesson covers Supervisor active-passive HA and primary-only audit/video persistence. This lesson covers the separate Collector data-ingestion tier, VRRP VIP ownership and job redistribution, not Supervisor database replication.

selected.lesson_subject: Simplified pre-logon tunnel: direct FortiSASE PoP machine-certificate authentication and post-login transition
selected.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiSASE 25.4.b simplified pre-logon uses a Windows machine certificate to establish a tunnel directly to the nearest FortiSASE Security PoP, replacing the earlier customer-managed FortiGate SSL/IPsec gateway path for new configurations.
selected.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: At boot, FortiClient selects a machine certificate matching both configured CN and Issuer (logical AND), validates against imported CA, connects to FortiSASE PoP and reaches AD destinations; after user login the pre-logon tunnel disconnects and the endpoint either autoconnects to Cloud Security tunnel or waits for manual tunnel selection.
selected.failure_class: Machine-certificate pre-logon session is established at PoP but immediately terminated or never appears connected due certificate selection/trust, destination policy, profile transition or IPsec parameter mismatch.
selected.evidence_pattern: Community report describes PoP showing connection success followed by termination while FortiClient never shows connected; multiple chains with/without intermediate CA did not resolve it and support case remained open. Configuration evidence includes CA, server cert, CN+Issuer AND matching, allowed destinations and endpoint profile toggle.
selected.remediation_path: Verify machine cert is staged before shipment, CA chain is imported, CN and Issuer filters both match the intended certificate, at least one FQDN/subnet destination is configured, endpoint profile enables pre-logon and global connection settings match. Compare inherited IPsec IKEv2 proposals/DPD/NAT-T with endpoint logs. Do not claim a confirmed root cause for the October 20 community case; it was unresolved at review.
selected.question_fingerprint: Trace a pre-logon tunnel that appears at the PoP but terminates on the endpoint, focusing on machine certificate matching and post-login transition.
selected.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Windows boot and machine certificate -> FortiSASE Security PoP -> allowed AD destination; user logon triggers disconnect and transition to separate user Cloud Security tunnel.
selected.semantic_uniqueness_review: Prior FortiSASE lessons cover concurrent IKEv2 multi-connect, branch on-ramp and security posture tags. They do not cover pre-user machine-certificate authentication, direct PoP tunnel establishment or the 25.4.b legacy-to-simplified transition.

selected.lesson_subject: FortiCloud Overlay-as-a-Service orchestration: per-device entitlement, FGFM transactions, rollback and ADVPN topology
selected.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiCloud OaaS is a subscription-based overlay provisioning controller for a single region and geo-redundant dual hub; an on-box OaaS agent uses the FGFM management tunnel to validate, compare and apply orchestrated FortiOS configuration as a transaction, rolling back the whole change set if any step fails.
selected.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Each FortiGate used by OaaS requires SWOS entitlement; FortiCloud portal builds hub/spoke topology; agent receives desired configuration over FGFM, validates and compares it, commits the FortiOS configuration transaction, or rolls back all orchestrated changes on failure; ADVPN hub informs spokes about better paths and shortcuts form directly between spokes.
selected.failure_class: Overlay provisioning task fails or is rolled back because of missing/expired SWOS entitlement, FGFM management tunnel failure, unsupported FortiOS version, UDP 500/4500/NAT-T reachability, or configuration conflict.
selected.evidence_pattern: System > FortiGuard license information shows Licensed/Expires Soon/Expired/Not Licensed; diagnose test update info lists SWOS; get oaas status reports Account, Site, Configuration version, Configuration sync status, Target version, Task ID and Error; verify IPsec tunnels, BGP routes, SLA and spoke-to-spoke ADVPN separately.
selected.remediation_path: Apply SWOS entitlement to every OaaS FortiGate; verify FortiOS 7.4.4+ and per-spoke license; confirm FGFM tunnel and UDP 500/4500 NAT-T reachability; inspect get oaas status and task error; validate IPsec/BGP/SD-WAN policy after commit. Distinguish the FortiCloud transaction/rollback workflow from FortiManager template installation and from ADVPN shortcut path discovery.
selected.question_fingerprint: Determine whether an OaaS task failure is entitlement, FGFM control-plane, config transaction or ADVPN data-plane and interpret get oaas status correctly.
selected.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: FortiCloud OaaS portal/controller to hub and spokes over FGFM management tunnels; on-box agent validates and commits/rolls back; separate hub/spoke ADVPN shortcuts show data-plane topology.
selected.semantic_uniqueness_review: Prior Secure SD-WAN records cover FortiManager overlay templates and ADVPN 2.0 edge discovery/path management. OaaS uses a FortiCloud subscription/controller, FGFM agent transaction and rollback; the lesson explicitly separates orchestration control plane from the already-covered ADVPN shortcut mechanics.
